title: Go: which habits still turn into vulnerabilities?
short: Rebuild every binary with Go 1.27.3 or 1.26.10 now and on each point release, gate CI on govulncheck and gosec, and put a timeout and a size limit on every request.
answer: Before your next release, rebuild every Go binary with Go 1.27.3 or 1.26.10, as Go 1.25 is unsupported[^policy][^release], and make `govulncheck` and `gosec` required CI checks. Judge everything else by whether outside data can reach SQL, a shell, a template, a path or a URL unchecked, or hold memory, a connection or a goroutine without a limit.
audience: Developers and tech leads writing production Go services and tools, and the security people who review them

blocks.title: If you only do five things

items.title: Run a supported Go and rebuild on every point release.
items.text: Only the two newest major releases get security fixes[^policy]: today 1.27.3 and 1.26.10[^release]. Rebuild to apply them; `go version -m` shows which Go built a binary[^emudhra].

items.title: Make govulncheck and gosec required checks.
items.text: `govulncheck ./...` narrows findings to vulnerabilities your code can reach and exits non-zero on them[^govulncheck]. gosec's taint rules G701 to G705 cover SQL, commands, paths, SSRF and XSS[^gosec].

items.title: Bound every request in time and size.
items.text: Zero `http.Server` timeouts mean none, and `http.DefaultClient` has none either[^nethttp]. Set `ReadHeaderTimeout`, wrap bodies in `http.MaxBytesReader` and time out every client.

items.title: Open files from input only through os.Root.
items.text: Path traversal ranks 6th in the CWE Top 25[^cwe]. `filepath.Join` cleans `..` but doesn't confine it[^filepath]; `os.OpenInRoot` and `os.Root` refuse names and symlinks that leave the directory[^ospkg].

items.title: Test with the race detector and fuzz your parsers.
items.text: Races on interfaces, maps, slices and strings can corrupt memory[^memmodel], and `go test -race` finds only those your tests execute[^race]. Give every parser a `go test -fuzz` target[^fuzz].

items.title: Where does outside data enter?
items.text: Find the handlers, gRPC methods and queue consumers it touches. Each should cap the body, decode into a struct and check the caller's right to the record: missing authorization ranks 4th in the CWE Top 25[^cwe].

items.title: Does it start a goroutine?
items.text: Ask what stops it, whether it gets the request's `context.Context` and what it shares without a lock[^memmodel].

items.title: Does input reach SQL, a command, a template or a path?
items.text: Search for `fmt.Sprintf` near `Query` or `Exec`, `"sh", "-c"`, `text/template`, `template.HTML(`, `filepath.Join`, `os.Open` and archive readers.

items.title: Does it call out over the network?
items.text: Check URLs from input, clients without a `Timeout`, `InsecureSkipVerify` and `ReverseProxy.Director`, deprecated in Go 1.26 because clients can strip the headers it adds[^go126].

items.title: Does it switch off Go's checks?
items.text: `unsafe`, cgo, `//go:debug` lines and `godebug` blocks in `go.mod` need a second reviewer.

blocks.title: Go traps and what to use instead
items: **`filepath.Join(dir, name)` and `http.Dir`.** `filepath.Join("a/b", "../../../xyz")` returns `../xyz`[^filepath], and `http.Dir` follows symlinks out of its tree and serves dotfiles such as `.git`[^nethttp]. Use `os.OpenInRoot`, `os.Root` and `http.FileServerFS(root.FS())`[^ospkg] on a tree without dotfiles, and patch: `os.Root` escapes were fixed in March, April, July and October[^osvulns][^rootchmod].

**`zip.NewReader` and `tar.NewReader`.** Both accept entry names like `../x` unless `GODEBUG` sets `zipinsecurepath=0` or `tarinsecurepath=0`[^godebug]. Create each entry through an `os.Root` and copy with `io.CopyN` to cap its size, as gosec G110 asks[^gosec].

**`text/template`, `template.HTML(s)` and data inside `<script>`.** Only `html/template` escapes, and it trusts template authors and `template.HTML` values[^htmltpl]. Go fixed seven `html/template` escaping bugs in 2026, five in script contexts[^tplvulns]. Pass data in `data-` attributes, and never parse templates from user input. Cross-site scripting ranks 1st in the CWE Top 25[^cwe].

**`db.Query(fmt.Sprintf(...))` and ORM string methods.** Go's docs call SQL built with `fmt` a security risk: pass values as arguments with your driver's placeholder, such as `?` or `$1`[^gosql]. GORM doesn't escape `Order`, `Select`, `Table`, `Group` or `Raw`, and `db.First(&u, id)` with a string `id` is injectable[^gorm]. Map sort columns from a fixed list.

**`exec.Command("sh", "-c", cmd)`.** `os/exec` deliberately runs no shell[^exec], and `sh -c` brings back OS command injection, 9th in the CWE Top 25[^cwe]. Pass each argument separately, put `--` before values that may start with `-`, and don't clear `exec.ErrDot`, which stops `Command` from resolving a name to a program in the current directory[^exec].

**`http.Get(r.FormValue("url"))`.** The default client has no timeout and follows up to 10 redirects[^nethttp]. Allowlist hosts, also in `CheckRedirect`, then reject loopback, private and link-local addresses in `net.Dialer.ControlContext`, which runs just before each connection is made[^net]. Server-side request forgery ranks 22nd in the CWE Top 25[^cwe].

**`json.Unmarshal(body, &req)`.** The v1 decoder matches names case-insensitively, lets the later of duplicate names win and ignores unknown fields, so two services can read one request differently[^jsonv2]. On Go 1.27, use `encoding/json/v2`, which rejects duplicates and invalid UTF-8 and matches names exactly, with `json.RejectUnknownMembers(true)`[^jsonv2].

**`go func() { ... }()` in a handler.** `net/http` recovers a panic in the handler itself[^nethttp], but an unrecovered panic in a goroutine it starts ends the program. Nil map writes, nil pointers, bad indexes and one-value type assertions all panic[^spec]. Use `v, ok := x.(T)` and a deferred `recover` in goroutines that handle input.

**`int32(n)` and other integer conversions.** They truncate with no indication of overflow, and arithmetic overflows without a panic[^spec]. Parse with the target size, as in `strconv.ParseInt(s, 10, 32)`, and check lengths before converting them, which gosec G115 flags[^gosec].

blocks.title: Tools that catch it
items: **govulncheck.** Source mode checks the standard library of the `go` on your `PATH`, `-mode binary` a built binary. Calls through `reflect` are invisible, and `-json` or `-format sarif` output never fails the build[^govulncheck].
**gosec.** Fix G112 (no `ReadHeaderTimeout`), G115 (integer conversion), G204, G304, G305, G402, G404 (`math/rand`) and G701 to G705 first[^gosec].
**Race detector and fuzzer.** `go test -race` can use 5 to 10 times the memory and 2 to 20 times the time[^race]: run it in CI. Fuzz one target per run with `-fuzztime`[^fuzz].
**Goroutine leak profile.** Go 1.27's `goroutineleak` profile reports goroutines that can never wake up[^go127].

blocks.title: What changed in 2026
items: **Go 1.27 shipped on 19 August,** ending support for Go 1.25[^release][^policy]. Old `go` lines no longer turn TLS 1.0 or 3DES back on by default[^go126][^go127].
**Go made its first URGENT release.** Go 1.27.3 and 1.26.10, out on 19 October, distrust eMudhra intermediates whose keys were trivially weak[^emudhra].

**Malicious proxies could bypass the checksum database** until fixes in May, August and October. Upgrade the installed Go, as pinning `GOTOOLCHAIN` isn't enough[^cmdgovulns]. The supply-chain sheet covers the rest.
**A compiler bug dropped bounds checks.** Go 1.26.2 and 1.25.9 fixed loop arithmetic that could let code without `unsafe` corrupt memory (CVE-2026-27143)[^cve27143].

blocks.title: What you can skip
items: **Setting `GOFLAGS=-mod=readonly`.** Build commands have behaved that way since Go 1.16[^gomod].
**FIPS 140-3 mode you don't need.** Go says applications without a compliance need shouldn't enable it, and `fips140=only` isn't meant for production[^fips].
**Rushing govulncheck's informational findings.** It lists vulnerabilities your code doesn't call separately and says you may not need to act[^govultut]. Fix them in routine updates.

blocks.title: Mistakes that cost the most
items: **Patching the image, not the binary.** On Linux, Go checks certificates itself, without revocation checks[^emudhra]. Binaries rebuilt with 1.27.3 or 1.26.10 reject the eMudhra intermediates whatever trust store the image ships[^emudhra]. Scan what you deploy with `govulncheck -mode binary`.

**Leaving the `go` line in `go.mod` behind.** Most GODEBUG defaults follow it, so a `go 1.23` module built with Go 1.27 still accepts RSA keys under 1,024 bits. Check with `go list -f '{{.DefaultGODEBUG}}'`[^godebug].

blocks.title: What this looks like for your code

columns.title: New project
items: Run `go get go@1.27.3` after `go mod init`, which writes an older `go` line[^go126], and use `encoding/json/v2` and `os.Root` from the start.
Give each `http.Server` timeouts, and put `http.NewCrossOriginProtection().Handler` in front of the mux against CSRF[^nethttp].
Make `govulncheck`, `gosec` and `go test -race` required checks.

columns.title: Existing codebase
items: Leave Go 1.25, raise the `go` line and compare `DefaultGODEBUG` before and after[^godebug].
Search for `ListenAndServe(`, `filepath.Join(`, `"sh", "-c"`, `InsecureSkipVerify`, `Director:` and `math/rand`.
Run `govulncheck -mode binary` on the binaries you deploy[^govulncheck].

columns.title: High-assurance or regulated
items: For FIPS 140-3, build with `GOFIPS140=certified`: Go Cryptographic Module v1.0.0 holds CMVP certificate #5247[^fips].
Fuzz every parser continuously; OSS-Fuzz runs native Go fuzz tests[^fuzz].
Require CodeQL's `security-extended` suite, and build releases with `CGO_ENABLED=0` unless a reviewed package needs cgo; `-race` needs it[^race].
